title: Handoff OSCORE master secrets survive in unzeroized CBOR buffers
description: Security review finding: OscoreState derives ZeroizeOnDrop, but OscoreState::to_cbor_entries clones master_secret/master_salt into ciborium::Value::Bytes, and HandoffResponse::encode serializes those secrets into a plain Vec<u8>. GatewayCoordinator wraps that plain Vec in CoapResponse and Gateway::dispatch_runtime_gcp retains it through OSCORE protection; neither the intermediate Value allocations nor the encoded plaintext payload are zeroized on drop. Successful and failed handoff response paths therefore leave node OSCORE key material in reusable heap memory despite the advertised secret lifecycle. Encode into Zeroizing buffers/secret-aware response ownership, avoid unnecessary clones, and ensure all intermediate plaintext CBOR allocations are wiped after protection or on every error; test drop/error paths with an instrumented allocator or explicit owned buffer hooks.
